## RNA-Seq Data

a1) Read the RNA-seq data

```{r}
fpkm_normalized <- read_csv(here("data", "_raw", "fpkm_table_normalized.csv"))
```

a2) Read the gene data

```{r}
genes_data <- read_csv(here("data", "_raw", "rows-genes.csv"))
```

a3) Read the sample data

```{r}
samples_data <- read_csv(here("data", "_raw", "columns-samples.csv"))
```

b\) Transpose df and rename sample id col

```{r}
rnaseq_transp <- fpkm_normalized |>
  rename(gene_id = 1) |>     # not necessary but easier than "gene_id\rnaseq_profile_id"
  column_to_rownames(var = "gene_id") |>    # we indicate that this is the header
  t() |> # we use to transpose because the data is too big for the pivot functions
  as_tibble(rownames = "rnaseq_profile_id") |>    # because t generates a matrix
  mutate(rnaseq_profile_id = as.numeric(rnaseq_profile_id))

```

c\) Rename gene cols

```{r}
identical(names(rnaseq_transp)[-1], as.character(genes_data$gene_id)) # Verify the gene IDs are in the exact same order

rnaseq_transp <- rnaseq_transp |>
  set_names(c("rnaseq_profile_id", make.unique(genes_data$gene_symbol)))
```

d-e) Add donor_id and structure acronym + Remove rnaseq id

```{r}
rnaseq_clean <- rnaseq_transp |>
  left_join(
    samples_data |> select(rnaseq_profile_id, donor_id, structure_acronym),
    by = "rnaseq_profile_id"
  ) |>
  select(-rnaseq_profile_id)
```

f\) Place the two added col in first position

```{r}
rnaseq_clean <- rnaseq_clean |>
  relocate(donor_id, structure_acronym)
```

g\) Save cleaned df

```{r}
write_tsv(rnaseq_clean, here("data", "03_rnaseq_clean.tsv.gz"))
```
